cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Find the Real Authority
cards.instruction: Probe until you know who can approve, block, or reverse the outcome.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll approve your repair arrangements when I know who can release the money for that leaking pipe.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've got all three signatures. Can I call the plumber?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not yet. You may have collected signatures from people who can't stop finance freezing it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Finance froze the roof payment too. Then the caretaker called, and they released it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You may call the caretaker first. Find out whether he can overrule finance or whether he knows someone who can. Then bring me the right name.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 makes approval conditional on discovering release authority; A3 refuses the requested plumber call and A5 authorizes the caretaker inquiry, so status governs the probe.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 signatures prompt A3 distinction between formal agreement and blocking power; B4 actual reversal supplies A5 next lead.

relationship.evidence: B2 has done the legwork and wants repair; B4 contributes useful experience rather than simply conceding to A.

heightening.evidence: B4 caretaker intervention causes A5 to distinguish personal override power from access to the real decision maker.

specificity.evidence: A1 leaking pipe and B2 plumber/signatures make repair funding legible; A5 asks about an unknown authority rather than inventing it.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 refuses a plumber call only for A5 to approve another investigative call; the bureaucratic delay is clear, with modest wit.
